headline: Iran offers Hormuz reopening in 7 days; oil under $100, BTC recovers to $86,190
summary: At 14:09 UTC on 22 September BTC is $86,189.70 against an $86,598.00 open, ETH $2,750.63 against $2,775.49 and SOL $117.47 against $118.90 - down 0.47%, 0.90% and 1.20% on the day but still up 12.7%, 12.5% and 17.4% on the week, and all three sit mid-range (BTC 46% up a $85,100.00-$87,446.70 band, ETH 39%, SOL 44%) after recovering from Asian-session lows rather than breaking down. The move that matters happened outside crypto: a senior Iranian official told Reuters on Tuesday that Iran can reopen the Strait of Hormuz within a week if the US eases military pressure and lifts its blockade of Iranian ports, which sent Brent 2.64% lower to $97.69 and WTI 3.20% lower to $89.41, while Saudi Aramco restarted its East-West pipeline and Yanbu exports resumed the same day. Lower crude weakens the case for further Fed tightening, and that is the channel through which this reached crypto - but the Fed is pushing the other way, with St Louis President Alberto Musalem saying on 21 September that more hikes may be needed because inflation is more likely to be substantially above 2% in 18 months without further restraint, ahead of Williams, Jefferson and Barkin today. Institutional demand is real and two-sided in size: US spot bitcoin ETFs took $998.95m on Monday 21 September (IBIT $381.4m, ARKB $289.1m, FBTC $238.8m), the largest day in about eleven months, and spot ether ETFs took roughly $270m with BlackRock's ETHA at $110m - but Hyperliquid open interest has rebuilt again on all three majors since the 10:24 UTC briefing (BTC $4.02bn from $3.92bn, ETH $3.18bn from $3.14bn, SOL $746m from $718m) with Fear & Greed at 78 in Extreme Greed. Today's dips are shallow, bought and news-free, so this reads as an extended market consolidating a 13% week, with the genuine event risk - Fed speakers today, flash PMIs tomorrow, the Xi summit Thursday - still ahead.

BTC.note: $86,189.70, only 0.47% under the open and 1.44% off the $87,446.70 high after bouncing from about $85,000 in the Asian session on the Hormuz headline, with funding flat and cheap at 0.00125%/h, the premium at 0.068% and Hyperliquid open interest at $4.02bn - up a third session in a row, so the tape is being re-leveraged rather than washed out.

ETH.note: $2,750.63, down 0.90% and sitting 39% up its $2,715.18-$2,806.69 range, with one genuine improvement since this morning: the futures premium has cooled back to 0.055% from 0.077% at 10:24 UTC even as open interest rose to $3.18bn, and spot ether ETFs bought roughly $270m on Monday led by ETHA's $110m, so the leverage build here is at least being paid for by real flow.

SOL.note: $117.47, the day's weakest at -1.20% and 2.08% under the $119.97 high but still the week's leader at +17.4%, with funding easing to 0.0013%/h from 0.00182%/h this morning and the thinnest book of the three at $746m of open interest, which keeps it the most reflexive in both directions into Alpenglow mainnet activation on 28 September.

drivers.title: Iran signals it can reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days
drivers.detail: A senior Iranian official told Reuters on Tuesday 22 September that Iran is ready to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within a week if the US eases military pressure and lifts its blockade of Iranian ports; Brent fell 2.64% to $97.69 - its first trip below $100 since 9 September - and WTI fell 3.20% to $89.41, with gasoline down 2.1% and heating oil down 3.1%. Saudi Aramco restarted its East-West pipeline at reduced rate the same day, shut since 13 September after drone attacks on pumping infrastructure, and Yanbu Red Sea exports resumed. This is an offer, not a reopening: only two commercial vessels transited on Monday against roughly 125 a day before the 28 February conflict, so the cheaper oil that is supporting risk assets can be taken back on one headline.

drivers.title: ETF bid is the strongest in eleven months: $998.95m into BTC funds, ~$270m into ETH
drivers.detail: US spot bitcoin ETFs took $998.95m of net inflow on Monday 21 September - the largest single day since October 2025 - led by BlackRock's IBIT at $381.4m, Ark's ARKB at $289.1m and Fidelity's FBTC at $238.8m, and spot ether ETFs took about $270m the same day with ETHA at $110m and Fidelity's FETH at $73.0m. That is roughly 12,000 BTC of regulated demand in one session and it is the single best argument that this week's advance has spot underneath it rather than only leverage; note the equity side did not follow, with MSTR and COIN both lower as bitcoin traded above $86,000.

drivers.title: The Fed is leaning hawkish into the oil relief: Musalem flags more hikes
drivers.detail: St Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem said on 21 September that further rate increases may be needed, that policy may still be stimulating the economy after the 16 September hike to 3.75-4.00%, and that without more restraint inflation is more likely to be substantially above the 2% target in 18 months than at target. New York's John Williams (14:05 UTC), Vice Chair Philip Jefferson (14:20 UTC) and Richmond's Thomas Barkin (17:00 UTC) speak today, with S&P Global flash PMIs tomorrow. The stored history flags this exact channel: 'inflation/CPI' headlines preceded a BTC dip within 6h 2.5% of the time versus 1.0% by chance (2.65x lift, n=118, held in both halves of the data), and the same combination with Trump's Truth Social posts ran at 2.6% versus 1.0% (2.67x, n=117).

drivers.title: Leverage is being rebuilt for a third session into an Extreme Greed tape
drivers.detail: Hyperliquid open interest rose again on all three majors in the roughly four hours since the last briefing - BTC $4.02bn from $3.92bn, ETH $3.18bn from $3.14bn, SOL $746m from $718m - while Fear & Greed sits at 78 in Extreme Greed and the composite reads 71.5 (momentum 81.9, crowding 63.9). Funding is still cheap at 0.00125%/h on BTC and ETH and premiums are modest at 0.055-0.077%, so this is not yet a crowded-long blow-off, but positioning has gone one way for three days into a market up 12.7-17.4% on the week and 24-hour liquidations have been running about 85-95% shorts, which means the pain trade has quietly flipped sides.

drivers.title: Xi at the White House Thursday, with a $14bn Taiwan arms package as the trip wire
drivers.detail: Xi Jinping meets Trump on 24 September in his first White House visit since 2015, with the Busan trade truce expiring 10 November and Beijing's commitments - at least 25 million tonnes of US soybeans a year through 2028 plus $17bn of other agricultural purchases - on the table alongside an AI safety notification mechanism. Beijing has warned through diplomatic channels, including a Kyodo News report, that it would cancel the summit if Washington approves a pending $14bn arms package for Taiwan before Xi arrives, so the binary here is a cancelled summit rather than a bad communique.

drivers.title: Crypto-native flow is constructive, with no live hack or depeg in the last 12 hours
drivers.detail: Binance disclosed a $100m stake in Circle - 1,237,011 Class A shares at $80.84, placement closed 17 September, locked for two years - alongside a five-year agreement to promote USDC, with Circle paying a monthly incentive fee on USDC held in Binance wallets. Separately the ECB and EU national central banks are seeking changes to MiCA's minimum bank-deposit rule for stablecoin reserves, and the ECB said it will put its own money into tokenised securities via the new Pontes DLT platform. None of this moves price today; the point is that there is no exploit, depeg or exchange failure in the last 12 hours, which is why news_risk sits at 45 rather than higher.

watch.what: New York Fed's John Williams, then Vice Chair Philip Jefferson at 14:20 UTC and Richmond's Thomas Barkin at 17:00 UTC. After Musalem's hawkish line yesterday, these are the most likely source of an intraday air pocket today - and the oil-driven easing in rate expectations is exactly what they could take back.
BitMEX shuts down permanently. Remaining balances and open positions have to move elsewhere - mechanical rather than directional, but a liquidity event.
US S&P Global flash PMI (euro area 08:00 UTC), the first full-month activity read since the 16 September hike. A hot services print is the cleanest bearish catalyst on the schedule.
Trump hosts Xi at the White House. Watch for a truce extension ahead of the 10 November expiry - and for the $14bn Taiwan arms package, which Beijing has said would cause it to cancel the meeting.
Iran's seven-day Hormuz window. If the US eases the port blockade the crude risk premium unwinds further; if talks stall, Brent goes back through $100 and the inflation trade returns with it.
Deribit quarterly options expiry, about $16.6bn notional ($14.73bn BTC, $1.92bn ETH), max pain near $72,000 - far below spot. Same day: Plasma's XPL cliff unlock of roughly $158m.

Solana's Alpenglow mainnet activation, cutting finality from about 12.8 seconds to 150 milliseconds. The largest protocol change of the quarter and the main asset-specific risk among the three majors.
BEA Personal Income and Outlays with the August PCE print, the cleanest test of the Fed's 2026 projections, on quarter-end when flows get pulled around.

Context for any deeper pullback, from the stored history: BTC dips during greed got +1.5% back in 7 of 7 cases, ETH in 92.9% of 28 and SOL in 93.8% of 48, with a typical extra drop after the trigger of -0.3% to -0.5% and a median time to recovery of 3.5-5.0 hours. Today's market state most resembles 2025-07-14, 2025-10-04 and 2019-05-05, after which BTC's median 30-day move was +8.8% (up in 60.0% of them).
